source_title: All the news from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event
source_excerpt:
Apple announced its first touchscreen MacBook at its “Pro and tell” event on October 28th. It’s the latest first from Apple, arriving just a couple of weeks after Apple debuted the HomeView , its first smart display, and a little over a month after it announced the iPhone Duo , its first foldable.
The Verge got a hands-on look at the touchscreen MacBook Pro following the event. It features Apple’s new “PROLED” XDR tandem OLED display, paired with an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip. It’s available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, starting at $2,899.
During the October 28th event, The Verge ’s Antonio Di Benedetto also got a hands-on look at the updated iPad Mini with a larger OLED display Apple announced on October 26th . In the lead-up to the event, Apple also refreshed the iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro with M6 chips. The company’s been on a streak of product launches since John Ternus took over as its CEO on September 1st. So far, the flurry of new devices has also included the iPhone 18 Pro , new Apple Watches , the AirPods 5 , and the HomePod Mini 2 .
Follow along here for all the latest news and updates.

Oct 30 Antonio G. Di Benedetto The touchscreen MacBook Pro is just a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen Touch ‘em if you got ‘em. Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Apple’s long-awaited touchscreen MacBook Pro is finally here. I got to try this MacBook that, according to the last two Apple CEOs , shouldn’t exist. The most surprising thing is how normal it is. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display (what a name) has one of the nicest screens I’ve seen on a laptop. The current Mini LED MacBook Pros are great, but the OLED has those even inkier blacks. It also gets super bright, with incredibly rich colors and infinite contrast. Apple calls it a “reference-caliber display,” which is a very Apple-y marketing term, but it walks the walk by being the first laptop display with support for Apple CMF 2026 color modes . Apple’s long-awaited touchscreen MacBook Pro is finally here. I got to try this MacBook that, according to the last two Apple CEOs , shouldn’t exist. The most surprising thing is how normal it is.
The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display (what a name) has one of the nicest screens I’ve seen on a laptop. The current Mini LED MacBook Pros are great, but the OLED has those even inkier blacks. It also gets super bright, with incredibly rich colors and infinite contrast. Apple calls it a “reference-caliber display,” which is a very Apple-y marketing term, but it walks the walk by being the first laptop display with support for Apple CMF 2026 color modes .
Oct 29 John Higgins Apple’s new laptop supports one of the coolest features for color pros Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge The new MacBook Pro brings with it a bunch of firsts for Apple laptops, the two flashiest being an OLED display and touchscreen functionality. But as an image-accuracy enthusiast, trained calibrator, and resident display expert, what excites me most about the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is the technology it uses to display an accurate picture. It’s the first laptop, and only the second product overall, to support Apple CMF 2026 color modes. It could be the future for displays. CMFs, or color-matching functions, mathematically represent how we perceive color, and there are a few different variations. The specification that’s been the standard for years is CIE 1931 (CIE stands for Commission Internationale de l’Éclairage, or International Commission on Illumination). For nearly a century, CIE 1931 has been a reliable calibration target, and most of the reference modes on the new MacBook use it. Read Article >

Oct 29 Tom Warren Apple finally combined a toaster and a refrigerator Image: Apple For more than 15 years, Apple has had a pretty simple answer to the idea of a touchscreen MacBook: no. Yesterday, Apple finally decided to think different and announce one anyway . “You’ve gotta touch it to believe it,” says Apple CEO John Ternus. He might be right: I haven’t yet touched it, and I still can’t quite believe it. Steve Jobs first called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible” in 2010, arguing that “touch surfaces don’t want to be vertical” and that using one for an extended period of time makes “your arm want to fall off.” He wasn’t wrong about the fatigue aspect of using a touchscreen laptop for long periods of time, but he missed the hybrid laptop opportunity Apple is now exploring. Oct 28 Terrence O'Brien and Antonio G. Di Benedetto Hands-on with Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro The difference in thickness is small compared to the non-touch MacBook Pro models. Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Steve Jobs famously called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible,” and for over a decade, Apple stridently refused to make one. Today that all changes with the MacBook Pro — the company’s first laptop to embrace a touch interface. While it’s unlikely that Apple can fix all the “terrible” ergonomics of having to lift your arm up and touch a laptop screen, the company has put some effort into making macOS more touch-friendly. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display weighs just 3 pounds, which is noticeably lighter than the current generation of non-touch MacBook Pros, which start at 3.4 pounds for the newly introduced M6 models . The difference is even bigger when you jump to the 16-inch model, which clocks in at 4 pounds, while the M5 Pro version without a touchscreen is 4.7. When picking up the 16-inch, you immediately notice the newfound lightness. It still has heft, but it feels better balanced when picking it up from a corner with one hand. Putting it side by side with a current 16-inch MacBook Pro, you see that it’s slightly thinner and has a footprint a smidge smaller. Aside from that, the feel of the materials is just like the MacBook Pros we’ve had for several years now. Read Article >

Oct 28 Jay Peters Apple announces its first touchscreen MacBook Pro Image: Apple Apple announced an all-new MacBook Pro laptop with an OLED touchscreen at its “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday. It starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model or $3,399 for the 16-inch version, and it’s available to preorder today ahead of its release on November 6th. The new MacBook Pro has what Apple calls a “PROLED XDR” display, which is a tandem OLED screen. It offers up to 2,000 nits of peak SDR brightness, up to a 120Hz refresh rate, and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. It’s equipped with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips — not the M6 chip on the other MacBook Pros announced this week. Apple announces its first touchscreen MacBook Pro
Apple announced an all-new MacBook Pro laptop with an OLED touchscreen at its “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday. It starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model or $3,399 for the 16-inch version, and it’s available to preorder today ahead of its release on November 6th.
The new MacBook Pro has what Apple calls a “PROLED XDR” display, which is a tandem OLED screen. It offers up to 2,000 nits of peak SDR brightness, up to a 120Hz refresh rate, and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. It’s equipped with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips — not the M6 chip on the other MacBook Pros announced this week. There’s a Dynamic Island on the screen that can show you things like Live Activities, similar to what’s available on iPhones. And the glowing Apple logo on the lid has returned.

And it’s never had a proper touchscreen. Photo by Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Apple has already had a busy week. On Monday, it announced a new iPad Mini with an upgraded OLED display , and on Tuesday, we got M6 chip upgrades for the MacBook Pro and iMac . The Macs are the definition of iterative updates — they’re quiet refreshes that look just like their direct predecessors. But today should be a whole lot more interesting. At an event in Los Angeles, Apple is expected to debut a revamped MacBook Pro with a touchscreen display . This would be the first touchscreen on a Mac (not counting the beleaguered Touch Bar ). Touchscreen laptops are something Apple executives have criticized for about as long as the iPad has existed. But after all this time, Apple is expected to give in to the growing demand to let people tap and swipe at a MacBook screen. Read Article >

Oct 27 Jess Weatherbed Apple refreshes the iMac with M6 chips This is the same marketing image Apple used for the M4 iMac, only the display on the far left now shows a different game. Image: Apple Apple is updating the iMac with M6 chips. The new iMac generation was introduced today, giving Apple’s all-in-one desktop computer a performance boost via the same chipset Apple launched with the Mac Mini in August . Prices start from $1,499, and the design otherwise appears largely unchanged. The update was announced ahead of Apple’s “Pro and Tell” event that’s scheduled to take place on Wednesday. This refresh comes two years after Apple gave the iMac an overhaul with M4 chips , meaning we’re skipping the M5 series entirely on this hardware. That should make this upgrade more meaningful. The M6 is Apple’s first 2nm chip and includes a dual 16-core Neural Engine that can boost performance when running on-device AI tasks.
